title: 🌍 UNIT 3: MANAGEMENT OF CONFLICT OVER RESOURCES
notes: Natural resources are essential for human livelihoods and economic development, but competition over scarce resources can create conflict.

title: 🌱 3.1 THE CONCEPT OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
notes:
Sustainable development → development that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

⭐ Main idea → balance human well-being, economic development and environmental protection.

Three major dimensions:
🔹 Economic → productive and sustainable economic activity.
🔹 Social → equity, quality of life and social well-being.
🔹 Environmental → conservation and sustainable use of natural resources.

title: 📜 3.1.1 HISTORICAL DEVELOPMENT OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
notes:
📅 1972 → Stockholm Conference → promoted environmental concern and led to the establishment of UNEP.

📅 1987 → sustainable development concept gained international prominence through the Brundtland Commission.

📅 1992 → Rio Earth Summit → developed Agenda 21 and strengthened links between poverty, development, environmental protection and resource management.

📅 2002 → Johannesburg World Summit → emphasized the social and economic dimensions of sustainable development.

📅 2015 → Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) adopted as global goals toward 2030.

title: 🎯 3.1.2 SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS
notes:
The SDGs are global goals designed to improve human well-being, protect the planet and promote prosperity and peace.

Major areas →
🔹 Poverty reduction
🔹 Food security
🔹 Health and education
🔹 Gender equality
🔹 Clean water and sanitation
🔹 Clean energy
🔹 Sustainable cities
🔹 Climate action
🔹 Biodiversity and ecosystem protection
🔹 Peace, justice and strong institutions

⭐ Target → achieve the goals by 2030.

title: 🇪🇹 3.1.3 SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT & ETHIOPIA
notes:
Ethiopian development priorities connect economic growth with poverty reduction, environmental protection and long-term resource sustainability.

Important directions include:
🔹 Agricultural development
🔹 Manufacturing and structural transformation
🔹 Productivity and competitiveness
🔹 Urban development
🔹 Human-resource and technological development
🔹 Climate-resilient green economy
🔹 Poverty reduction
🔹 Improved governance

⭐ Sustainable development requires economic progress together with environmental and social responsibility.

title: ⚠️ 3.1.4 CHALLENGES OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
notes:
Major challenges include:

🔹 Different interpretations of sustainable development.

🔹 Difficulty applying one approach to different societies and environments.

🔹 Conflicts between economic growth and environmental protection.

🔹 Unequal distribution of development benefits.

🔹 Different social, cultural and political priorities.

⭐ Effective sustainable development requires balancing environmental, economic and social interests.

title: 💧 3.2 RESOURCE USE POLICIES & RELATED CONFLICTS
notes:
Resource → any element or substance useful for satisfying human needs.

Natural resources are classified according to their ability to regenerate:

♻️ Renewable resources → can replenish themselves within a foreseeable period.
Examples → water, forests, soil, vegetation, animals and solar energy.

⛏️ Non-renewable resources → form very slowly and have limited natural supplies.
Examples → coal, petroleum, natural gas and mineral resources.

title: ⚔️ 3.2.1 RESOURCE CONFLICTS
notes:
Resource conflict → disagreement or competition over ownership, access, control, management or benefits from natural resources.

Common resources involved →
💧 Water
🌳 Forests
🌾 Land
🐄 Rangelands
⛏️ Minerals
🛢️ Oil and gas
🐟 Fisheries

Four major conflict areas:
1️⃣ Resource ownership
2️⃣ Resource access
3️⃣ Resource-management decisions
4️⃣ Distribution of resource benefits and burdens.

title: 🌍 3.2.2 CHARACTERISTICS OF RESOURCE CONFLICTS
notes:
Resource conflicts are often complex because:

🔹 Resources are unevenly distributed geographically.
🔹 Availability can change because of natural and social factors.
🔹 Different groups may depend on the same resource.
🔹 Resource disputes may involve ethnic, religious or linguistic differences.
🔹 Multiple actors may be involved.
🔹 Conflicts may occur at local, national or transboundary levels.

⭐ Resource conflict is not automatically destructive; peaceful conflict management can support positive change.

title: 📉 3.2.3 RESOURCE SCARCITY
notes:
Resource scarcity → available renewable resources are insufficient to satisfy local demand.

Three major types:

1️⃣ Demand-induced scarcity → demand increases faster than available supply.

Causes → population growth + increased consumption + new technologies.

2️⃣ Supply-induced scarcity → total resource supply decreases because of environmental degradation, natural variation or infrastructure failure.

3️⃣ Structural scarcity → different groups have unequal access to resources because of social, economic, cultural or institutional barriers.

title: 🏛️ 3.2.4 MAIN DRIVERS OF RESOURCE CONFLICT
notes:
Three major drivers:

1️⃣ Competition over increasingly scarce renewable resources.

2️⃣ Poor governance of renewable resources and the environment.

3️⃣ Transboundary natural-resource pressures and interactions.

⭐ These drivers can combine with political, economic and security pressures to increase conflict.

title: 🌾 3.2.5 LIVELIHOOD RESPONSES TO RESOURCE SCARCITY
notes:
Communities can reduce vulnerability to resource scarcity through:

🔹 Livelihood diversification → combine agricultural and non-agricultural activities.

🔹 Efficiency improvement → increase production and add value through technology, inputs, processing and manufacturing.

🔹 Livelihood adaptation → adjust activities to declining resource availability, climate change and disasters.

🔹 Livelihood protection → protect food security, income, employment and natural capital.

🔹 Emergency support → food, water, sanitation, shelter and health services when livelihoods fail.

title: 🌊 3.2.6 TRANSBOUNDARY RESOURCE CONFLICTS
notes:
Transboundary resources → natural resources shared across national borders.

Examples →
💧 Rivers and water
🐟 Fisheries
🦌 Wildlife
🌬️ Air quality

Conflict may arise when:
🔹 One country uses a shared resource disproportionately.
🔹 Pollution crosses borders.
🔹 Land-use changes in one country affect another.
🔹 Pastoralists and wildlife cross national boundaries.
🔹 Illegal extraction and trade affect resource-dependent communities.

⭐ Cooperation and co-management are important for shared resources.

title: 🇪🇹 3.2.7 WATER RESOURCE CONFLICTS & ETHIOPIA
notes:
Water is a major transboundary resource in the Horn of Africa.

🔹 Rivers cross or form borders between countries.
🔹 Different countries may have competing interests in water use.
🔹 Dams and irrigation projects can create disagreements over water allocation and management.

⭐ Sustainable management requires cooperation, equitable use, consultation and consideration of the interests of affected communities.

title: 🌿 3.3 GOVERNANCE OF NATURAL RESOURCES
notes:
Natural resource governance → the institutions, rules, processes and relationships that determine how natural-resource power, responsibilities, decisions, access and benefits are managed.

Good governance should promote:
🔹 Environmental sustainability
🔹 Social equity
🔹 Public participation
🔹 Transparency
🔹 Clear resource rights
🔹 Community involvement
🔹 Accountability
🔹 Conservation

⭐ Effective governance can reduce resource-related conflicts and protect livelihoods.

title: ⚠️ 3.3.1 GOVERNANCE CHALLENGES
notes:
Four major governance problems can contribute to resource conflict:

1️⃣ Unclear, overlapping or poorly enforced resource rights and laws.

2️⃣ Discriminatory policies, rights and laws that marginalize particular groups.

3️⃣ Unequal distribution of development benefits and environmental burdens.

4️⃣ Lack of public participation and transparency in decision-making.

⭐ Weak governance increases competition, grievances and vulnerability.

title: ✅ 3.3.2 PRINCIPLES OF GOOD NATURAL RESOURCE GOVERNANCE
notes:
Important approaches include:

🔹 Clarify resource rights, responsibilities and institutional mandates.

🔹 Ensure equitable access to renewable resources, especially for poor and marginalized groups.

🔹 Require environmental and social impact assessments for major projects.

🔹 Make impact assessments transparent and involve affected stakeholders.

🔹 Increase public participation in resource-management decisions.

🔹 Promote community-based and collaborative management.

⭐ Good governance → clear rights + fairness + participation + transparency + environmental responsibility.

title: 🤝 3.3.3 COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
🧑🏾‍🌾 3.4 INDIGENOUS CONFLICT RESOLUTION PRACTICES
notes:
Indigenous conflict resolution → traditional community-based methods used to prevent, manage and resolve disputes.

Characteristics:
🔹 Based on customs and traditions.
🔹 Often led by respected elders or traditional leaders.
🔹 Passed from generation to generation.
🔹 Rooted in community values and relationships.
🔹 Emphasizes reconciliation and peaceful coexistence.

⭐ Indigenous mechanisms often operate alongside formal legal systems.

title: 👴🏾 3.4.1 ROLE OF ELDERS
notes:
Shimagle / elders → respected people who help settle disputes within communities.

Their roles may include:
🔹 Hearing both sides.
🔹 Mediating disagreements.
🔹 Encouraging forgiveness.
🔹 Restoring social relationships.
🔹 Negotiating compensation.
🔹 Preventing revenge and further conflict.

⭐ Community trust and respect for elders strengthen the effectiveness of traditional mediation.

title: 🇪🇹 3.4.2 ETHIOPIAN INDIGENOUS SYSTEMS
notes:
Ethiopia has diverse indigenous conflict-resolution systems associated with different communities.

🔹 Oromo → Gadaa system.
🔹 Amhara → Shimagle / elders.
🔹 Somali → T’eer and Guurti elders.
🔹 Afar → Mada’a system.

Traditional institutions are based on orally transmitted customs and differ among ethnic groups.

title: ⚖️ 3.4.3 PASTORAL CONFLICT RESOLUTION
notes:
Pastoral communities have traditional institutions for managing disputes over land, pasture, water and other resources.

🔹 Somali → Ogaz and Guurti elders.
🔹 Borana/Oromo → Abbaa Gadaa and Gadaa institutions.
🔹 Afar → Kedo Abba and Mada’a.

Two broad areas of customary law:
🔹 Intra-ethnic disputes → conflicts within a group.
🔹 Inter-ethnic disputes → conflicts between different groups.

title: 🕊️ 3.4.4 GUMMA & RECONCILIATION
notes:
Gumma → Oromo conflict-resolution practice particularly associated with cases involving killing.

🔹 Helps prevent revenge and continuing grievances.
🔹 Encourages reconciliation between affected groups.
🔹 Recognizes relationships between individuals, families and clans.

⭐ Indigenous approaches often seek restoration of relationships rather than only punishment.

title: 🌐 3.4.5 INDIGENOUS RIGHTS & CONFLICT RESOLUTION
notes:
The UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples recognizes important rights related to:

🔹 Land and self-determination.
🔹 Freedom, peace and security.
🔹 Protection from violence.
🔹 Consultation concerning indigenous lands and territories.
🔹 Participation in decisions concerning development and resource use.
🔹 Fair procedures for resolving conflicts and protecting rights.

⭐ Respect for indigenous rights supports peaceful resource management.

title: ⚖️ 3.4.6 INDIGENOUS VS FORMAL CONFLICT RESOLUTION
🧠 UNIT 3 KEY DIFFERENCES
notes:
🌱 Sustainable development → meet present needs while protecting future generations.

♻️ Renewable resource → naturally replenishable within a foreseeable period.
⛏️ Non-renewable resource → limited resource that forms very slowly.

⚔️ Resource conflict → disagreement over resource ownership, access, control, management or benefits.

📉 Demand-induced scarcity → demand increases.
🏜️ Supply-induced scarcity → supply decreases.
⚖️ Structural scarcity → unequal access between groups.

🏛️ Natural resource governance → rules and institutions controlling resource decisions and benefits.

🤝 Indigenous conflict resolution → community-based traditional methods emphasizing mediation and reconciliation.

title: ⭐ UNIT 3 QUICK REVISION
notes:
🌱 Sustainable development → present needs + future generations.

🌍 Three dimensions → economic + social + environmental.

🎯 SDGs → global development goals toward 2030.

♻️ Renewable → replenishable.

⛏️ Non-renewable → limited and slowly formed.

⚔️ Resource conflict → ownership + access + decision-making + benefit distribution.

📉 Resource scarcity → insufficient supply for demand.

🔺 Scarcity types → demand-induced + supply-induced + structural.

🏛️ Main conflict drivers → scarcity + poor governance + transboundary pressures.

🌊 Transboundary resources → water + fisheries + wildlife + air.

🌾 Livelihood responses → diversification + efficiency + adaptation + protection + emergency support.

🌿 Good governance → clear rights + equity + transparency + participation + impact assessment.

👴🏾 Indigenous resolution → elders + customs + mediation + reconciliation.

🇪🇹 Key systems → Gadaa + Shimagle + T’eer + Mada’a + Gumma.

🤝 Main goal → peaceful, equitable and sustainable management of natural resources.
